title: Perplexity Decider v1.3 Adds Locate for Decision Tasks
summary: Perplexity releases Decider v1.3 and Flash v1.3, open-weight decision models with Locate for span extraction. Achieves 91.6% accuracy on 63 tasks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Perplexity released Decider v1.3 and Flash v1.3, open-weight models that return probabilities for query classification, not text generation.
- Version 1.3 introduces Locate, a new capability for extracting text spans, expanding decision model use cases beyond binary classification.
- Decider v1.3 reports 91.6% mean accuracy across 63 query-classification benchmarks, positioning it as a specialized tool for routing and filtering.


Perplexity AI has officially launched Decider v1.3 and Flash v1.3, a new generation of[open-weight](https://emergent.sh/glossary/open-source-model)[decision models](https://emergent.sh/news/hugging-face-launches-decision-models-hub-ai) designed to return probabilities rather than text. Officially released on November 13, 2026, version 1.3 introduces Locate, a span-extraction capability that extends the models beyond binary classification into structured information retrieval. With a reported 91.6% mean accuracy across 63 query-classification tasks, these models represent a specialized approach to AI inference, optimizing for routing, filtering, and structured decision-making rather than open-ended language generation.


## What Are Decision Models?


Unlike traditional large language models that generate human-readable text, decision models output discrete probabilities or structured predictions. Perplexity's Decider v1.3 and Flash v1.3 are trained to classify queries, route requests, and extract spans of text based on predefined logic. This architecture makes them ideal for tasks like intent detection, content moderation, search relevance scoring, and entity extraction. By returning probabilities instead of prose, these models reduce latency and computational overhead in production environments where classification speed matters more than generation quality.


The open-weight release allows developers to audit, fine-tune, and deploy the models on-premises or in private clouds. This transparency aligns with the growing demand for verifiable AI systems in regulated industries.


## Locate: Span Extraction for Structured Data


Version 1.3 introduces Locate, a feature that enables the model to identify and extract specific text spans from input documents. For example, given a customer support query, Locate can pinpoint product names, error codes, or policy references without generating explanatory text. This capability is particularly useful in workflows that require structured outputs, such as populating database fields, tagging documents, or feeding downstream automation pipelines.


Locate expands the decision model paradigm beyond yes/no classification into nuanced information retrieval. Developers can now use a single model for both routing ("Is this a refund request?") and extraction ("Which order number does this reference?").


## Performance Benchmarks


Perplexity reports that Decider v1.3 achieves 91.6% mean accuracy across 63 query-classification benchmarks. These tasks include intent detection, sentiment analysis, topic categorization, and entity recognition. While the company has not disclosed per-task breakdowns, the aggregate score suggests strong performance on structured prediction workloads.


- 91.6% mean accuracy on 63 classification tasks
- Open-weight release enables reproducibility and custom fine-tuning
- Span extraction via Locate for structured information retrieval


Flash v1.3, the smaller and faster variant, is designed for latency-sensitive applications where inference speed is critical. Both models share the same architectural improvements introduced in v1.3, including better calibration of probability outputs and more robust handling of ambiguous queries.


## Availability and Use Cases


Decider v1.3 and Flash v1.3 are available now as open-weight releases. Developers can download the models from Perplexity's distribution channels for local deployment or integration into existing AI pipelines. The models are licensed for commercial use, with weights and evaluation scripts provided for transparency.


Primary use cases include customer support automation, content moderation at scale, search query understanding, and multi-stage retrieval pipelines. The Locate feature is expected to see adoption in knowledge base systems, document processing workflows, and compliance scanning tools where extracting structured data from unstructured text is a bottleneck.


## What This Means


Perplexity Decider v1.3 and Flash v1.3 signal a maturation of decision models as a distinct category of AI inference. By prioritizing probability outputs over text generation, these models offer a leaner alternative for classification and extraction tasks that do not require generative capabilities. The addition of Locate broadens the addressable use cases, positioning decision models as a complement to, rather than a replacement for, large language models in production AI stacks. For teams building query routers, intent classifiers, or document processors, v1.3 provides a transparent, performant option backed by public benchmarks and open weights.
